lead: >-
  Adventure takes different forms across this country combination:
  walking trails around Iguazu Falls, a ferry crossing over the Río de
  la Plata to Montevideo, and an excursion to El Peñón rock near Guatapé.
  The off-road jeep section, however, takes place in Bolivia, outside
  this three-country filter. Compare the physical demands and actual
  limitations of the extended itinerary.

## Where the active parts of the trip take place

Our selection includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}}. One current option is the [32-day tour of eight South American countries](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/), which visits Argentina, Colombia and Uruguay. The itinerary also includes Brazil, Chile, Bolivia, Peru and Ecuador. Selecting three countries in the catalogue **does not create a separate, shortened journey** or mean that those countries are visited consecutively.

Three different ways of travelling distinguish this combination. At Iguazu, visitors explore the falls using the national park's developed walking routes. In Uruguay, they take a ferry from Buenos Aires to Montevideo and return the same day. In Colombia, a road excursion leads from Medellín to Guatapé and El Peñón rock. None of these stages amounts to a sporting trek in its own right.

The most distinctly adventurous section of the full tour comes later: **a two-day 4×4 jeep journey through the Bolivian highlands** after Chile's Atacama Desert. This is important when assessing the difficulty: the adventure theme belongs to the whole eight-country itinerary, not necessarily to every country selected in the filter. For other combinations without a theme, explore [Argentina, Colombia and Uruguay](/multi-country/argentina_colombia_uruguay/), or see the [international adventure catalogue](/multi-country/interests/adventure/) for more active trips.

## Iguazu in Argentina: walking trails rather than rafting

The Argentine day takes place around [Puerto Iguazú](/argentina/place/puerto-iguazu/) and the waterfalls on the Iguazu River. The tour includes a group excursion with a Russian-speaking guide. Visitors can see the humid forest and powerful cascades from established visitor trails, but **white-water rafting, canyoning and camping treks are not listed for the Argentine section**.

On the neighbouring Brazilian side, Macuco Safari is mentioned separately as an optional paid activity. It must not be treated as an included part of the Argentine excursion. Water levels affect access to certain viewpoints. In 2026, the Argentine park administration temporarily restricted access to the Devil's Throat trail because of flooding, so trail conditions should be checked before the actual visit.

After the falls, the group flies to [Buenos Aires](/argentina/place/buenos-aires/). The city tour and an evening tango show belong to the cultural part of the journey. Travellers who want to spend more time exploring Argentina's landscapes can compare the [Argentina adventure tours](/interests/adventure/tours/argentina/) by days, modes of travel and genuine physical activities.

## Uruguay: ferry crossing and a walk around Montevideo

Uruguay is allocated **one full-day excursion**. Early in the morning, the group departs Buenos Aires for the port, crosses to [Montevideo](/uruguay/place/montevideo/) and explores the city with an English-speaking guide. The port, Independence Square, the old town and the cathedral are followed by free time. The group returns along the same route in the evening. Ferry tickets are included in the stated services.

It is a busy sightseeing day, but not an adventure in the sense of off-roading or hiking. **The Río de la Plata ferry is not a wildlife-watching cruise**, and a short visit to the capital does not justify promising Uruguayan national parks, mountain treks or beach holidays. Adding nature activities in Uruguay would require changes to the original schedule and a separately agreed programme.

When planning this part of the journey, allow not only for sightseeing in Montevideo but also for the journey to the port, boarding formalities, the crossing itself and the return to the Argentine hotel. Travel documents and border rules need to be checked for every participant's nationality. Weather and the ferry timetable may also affect the day's order of activities.

## Colombia: a rock, a lake and an eight-hour excursion

In Colombia, the day closest to the adventure theme is an excursion from [Medellín](/colombia/place/medellin/) to [El Peñón de Guatapé](/colombia/place/el-penon-de-guatape/), [Guatapé](/colombia/place/guatape/) and the reservoir. The excursion lasts **8 hours** and includes an English-speaking guide, a visit to a replica of old El Peñol and streets lined with decorated façades.

The rock is famous for its stairway to the summit, but **visiting the monolith and being required to climb the steps are different conditions**. The published tour does not confirm that the climb is included for every guest. Anyone wishing to make the ascent should clarify access, time at the stop and the physical demands. Part of the eight-hour excursion is spent in transport, so it should not be described as an eight-hour hike.

Afterwards, the programme includes [Cartagena](/colombia/place/cartagena/), [Bogotá](/colombia/place/bogota/) and [Monserrate](/colombia/place/monserrate-bogota/). A trip up Monserrate is included in Bogotá, but the programme does not describe an independent sporting ascent along the trail. Much of the Colombian leg is devoted to cities and historic sightseeing rather than extreme sports. Other options are available in the [Colombia adventure tours](/interests/adventure/tours/colombia/).

## The real off-road section is in Bolivia

Travellers choosing this itinerary primarily for its active component should look beyond the three countries in the filter heading. After San Pedro de Atacama, the full tour includes **two days in four-wheel-drive jeeps** through Bolivia's high-altitude lagoons, geothermal areas and the Uyuni salt flats. Some sections are above 4,000 metres, and the programme explicitly identifies the risk of altitude sickness.

The demands are quite different from Iguazu's paths, a walk through Montevideo or a road excursion to Guatapé. Suitable warm clothing, sun protection and an assessment of your tolerance for altitude are needed. Travelling by jeep does not eliminate long periods on uneven roads or the effects that altitude may have on well-being.

When comparing options, consider three things: how many hours are spent travelling, where physical activity actually takes place, and whether a demanding section could be replaced by a gentler alternative. Ada Tours can help clarify the order of transfers and discuss a more comfortable pace where compatible with the confirmed programme. Specific medical concerns should be discussed with a doctor rather than settled by promotional promises.

## What changes across climates and borders

| Section | Practical consideration |
|---|---|
| Iguazu | Humidity, trails and water |
| Montevideo | Ferry and border crossing |
| Guatapé | Long excursion and steps |
| Bolivia | Altitude and off-road travel |

In Argentina, the journey begins among humid waterfalls and continues to Buenos Aires. For the one-day visit to Uruguay, weather around the Río de la Plata estuary and the ferry schedule matter. The Colombian leg takes in mountainous Medellín, warm Cartagena and high-altitude Bogotá. What you pack for one stop will not cover all the others, and the full tour also includes the dry Atacama and cold highland nights.

Travel documents need to be checked for **all eight countries on the route** and the transit airports, not just the three selected. Their currencies also differ: Argentine pesos, Uruguayan pesos and Colombian pesos. Whether a particular foreign bank card or US dollars can be used depends on the location, bank and current restrictions. Before payment and departure, it is wise to agree on backup payment methods, insurance and baggage requirements for domestic flights.

The principal commercial terms are provided on the full tour page: prices and included services apply to the entire programme, not to individual three-country sections.

{{catalog.tourTable:tour_south_america_eight_countries_32_days_2026}}

## Frequently asked questions about adventure in Argentina, Colombia and Uruguay

### Is extreme rafting at Iguazu included in Argentina?

The confirmed Argentine section includes a group visit to the waterfalls. Extreme rafting is not listed. Macuco Safari on the Brazilian side is offered separately for an additional charge.

### Is the visit to Uruguay an adventure tour?

It is a full one-day ferry trip and sightseeing excursion in Montevideo. The Uruguayan leg is not advertised as a sporting or nature-expedition programme.

### Is climbing El Peñón in Colombia mandatory?

There is no confirmation that the staircase ascent is included for everyone. The description includes a visit to the rock and Guatapé; the possibility of climbing should be agreed separately.

### Where does the off-road section take place?

In Bolivia, after Chile's Atacama Desert. The complete trip includes two days in 4×4 jeeps across high-altitude terrain.

### Can I visit only the three countries in the filter?

This page shows an intersection of countries within a current eight-country itinerary. A separate shorter trip would need to be designed and agreed as a different route.

## From Río de la Plata tango to Caribbean coastal history

Our selection includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} involving Argentina, Colombia and Uruguay with a focus on culture and history. One suitable current option is a [32-day journey through eight South American countries](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/). The selected countries are part of **a much longer sequence**, not a separate three-country journey: after Argentina and a one-day visit to Uruguay, the route continues through Chile, Bolivia, Peru and Ecuador before reaching Colombia.

The appeal of this combination is the chance to encounter distinct cultural worlds. Buenos Aires and Montevideo are linked by the history of their ports, migration and tango. Cartagena showcases Spanish colonial architecture and the defensive works of the Caribbean coast. Bogotá adds pre-Columbian gold, a colonial city centre and works by Fernando Botero; Medellín brings art and the urban transformations of recent decades.

The three destinations do not receive equal amounts of time, however: **Uruguay has a single day excursion**, Argentina includes Iguazu Falls and Buenos Aires, and Colombia features several cities and museums. When choosing, compare the time actually spent in each place rather than simply counting countries on a map. If you do not need a themed filter, explore the [general Argentina + Colombia + Uruguay selection](/multi-country/argentina_colombia_uruguay/); other cultural itineraries appear in the [multicountry culture and history catalogue](/multi-country/interests/culture-and-history/).

## Buenos Aires: neighbourhoods, squares and an evening of tango

The Argentine cultural leg begins after the visit to the waterfalls near [Puerto Iguazú](/argentina/place/puerto-iguazu/). In [Buenos Aires](/argentina/place/buenos-aires/), a three-hour sightseeing tour with a Russian-speaking guide is scheduled. It covers La Boca, San Telmo, Recoleta, Puerto Madero and other central attractions. This offers an introduction to the city, but three hours of sightseeing cannot be equated with an in-depth exploration of all its museums and historic neighbourhoods.

An evening **tango show with dinner** is included. Tango forms an especially fitting cultural bridge between Argentina and Uruguay: UNESCO has inscribed tango as intangible cultural heritage shared by Buenos Aires and Montevideo. The dance developed in the urban communities of the Río de la Plata, absorbing many different influences. An evening in Buenos Aires therefore provides a meaningful connection to Montevideo, which the group visits the next day.

Nevertheless, the confirmed itinerary includes **a tango show only in Buenos Aires**. No separate dance evening is scheduled during the Montevideo excursion. To explore music venues in both cities and compare their traditions firsthand, more free time and a different visiting schedule would be required.

## Montevideo: one day in the historic centre

Early in the morning, the group travels from the Argentine capital to the port and crosses the Río de la Plata by ferry. After reaching [Montevideo](/uruguay/place/montevideo/), an English-speaking guide leads a city tour. The programme lists the port, Independence Square, the old town and the cathedral. Free time follows, then the return crossing and a transfer to the Buenos Aires hotel. **Ferry tickets are included** in the stated programme.

For a historically minded traveller, Montevideo offers an interesting contrast: a more compact and unhurried waterfront centre, different urban architecture and its own national history. Comparing the public spaces of the two capitals, their old port districts and the growth of two cities linked by the same estuary is particularly rewarding.

Time is the main limitation. The ferry crossing and return take up a considerable share of the day. The itinerary includes **no overnight stay in Uruguay, excursion to Colonia del Sacramento or separate winery visit**. That is an important difference between a full cultural journey through Uruguay and an introduction to one capital. If Uruguay is your principal destination, it makes more sense to allocate additional days than to try to fit everything into the existing one-day excursion.

## Medellín: urban art and Comuna 13

The Colombian leg begins with a flight from Guayaquil to [Medellín](/colombia/place/medellin/). After visiting El Peñón rock and [Guatapé](/colombia/place/guatape/), the programme includes an excursion through Medellín and Comuna 13. This neighbourhood is often cited as an example of how street art and cultural spaces have contributed to rethinking a city's difficult past.

Comuna 13 is a place of real social histories. Visiting it is best approached through a guide's explanations and respect for residents, rather than treating striking graffiti merely as a photographic backdrop. A flight to Cartagena follows the city excursion, so it would be unwise to assume that an entire free evening in Medellín is available.

The separate day trip to Guatapé presents another kind of architecture: vividly painted house façades and a replica of old El Peñol. These can be compared with Medellín's contemporary street art, although the Guatapé excursion combines cultural and natural attractions.

## Cartagena: walls, fortress and old town

A **four-hour** sightseeing tour of [Cartagena](/colombia/place/cartagena/) with a Russian-speaking guide is scheduled. Sights include the bay, the old city gates with their clock tower, historic neighbourhoods, San Felipe de Barajas Fortress, the Church of San Pedro Claver and old squares. The exact arrangements for stops and entering particular sites should be checked against the excursion description: viewing a landmark from outside and visiting its interior are different services.

Cartagena's historic port and fortifications are inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List. The walls and bastions reflect the city's role in colonial trade and in defending maritime routes. They offer a tangible contrast with the Río de la Plata: two coastal worlds in South America with different architecture and historical development.

If free hours really remain after the guided tour, an unhurried evening walk through the historic streets is a good use of them. This Cartagena itinerary does not promise a separate beach day or an island excursion.

## Bogotá: pre-Columbian art and the historic centre

In [Bogotá](/colombia/place/bogota/), the programme covers La Candelaria, the Gold Museum, the Botero collection and historic squares, as well as a visit up [Monserrate](/colombia/place/monserrate-bogota/). The following day includes a trip to the **Salt Cathedral of Zipaquirá**, where architecture and the history of salt mining meet in an unusual underground setting.

This section is particularly interesting for travellers looking beyond colonial façades to understand the region's earlier civilisations. The Gold Museum displays pre-Columbian works, while the historic centre shows how successive periods of city life have left their mark. The Monserrate excursion adds a panoramic view of the capital from above, but does not include an independent sporting ascent by mountain trail.

Museums may have different closing days and access requirements. If a visit to **a particular collection** is essential, check its opening schedule for your travel dates. It is not safe to assume that every museum opens every day; the excursion sequence should be agreed in advance, especially with fixed flights and a busy itinerary.

## Combining historic cities without wasting time

| Country | What is actually included |
|---|---|
| Argentina | Buenos Aires, sightseeing and tango |
| Uruguay | One day in Montevideo |
| Colombia | Medellín, Cartagena, Bogotá, Zipaquirá |

There are three practical decisions to make. First, identify the cultural experience that matters most: tango and the cities of the Río de la Plata, colonial fortresses on the Caribbean coast, or Bogotá's pre-Columbian collections. Second, assess travel days: four other countries lie between Uruguay and Colombia on this full tour, so there is no direct ferry or short flight between these two stops. Third, consider the actual languages of the guides: Russian-speaking guiding is listed for sightseeing in Buenos Aires and Cartagena, whereas the Montevideo guide speaks English.

The eight-country itinerary and its dynamically presented commercial terms are shown below. They apply **to the entire journey**, not to an isolated combination of three countries:

{{catalog.tourTable:tour_south_america_eight_countries_32_days_2026}}

For someone interested exclusively in the culture of these three countries, the original full route may be too long: it also includes nature and high-altitude stages elsewhere. For travellers who want museums, tango, colonial neighbourhoods and the wider cultural diversity of South America, that broader sequence offers more context.

## Frequently asked questions about culture in Argentina, Colombia and Uruguay

### Is tango included, and in which country?

A tango show with dinner is scheduled in Buenos Aires. Tango is a cultural tradition shared by Argentina and Uruguay, but a separate tango show in Montevideo is not included here.

### Can we visit Colonia del Sacramento?

The confirmed Uruguayan programme includes one day in Montevideo followed by a return to Buenos Aires. Colonia del Sacramento is not included; such an extension would need to be arranged separately.

### Does the Cartagena excursion include a fortress visit?

San Felipe de Barajas Fortress is listed among the sights on the four-hour tour. Admission to the interior, tickets and the length of the stop should be checked against the detailed excursion programme.

### Which stops are best for discovering Colombian history?

On this tour, Cartagena introduces the country's colonial maritime history, Bogotá offers pre-Columbian art, its historic centre and Monserrate, while Medellín introduces contemporary urban culture. These are successive stops with distinct themes.

### Can all three countries be visited on a short trip?

This specific current tour is a complete eight-country itinerary, not a short combination. A shorter option would require a separate programme with different flights and a different distribution of days.

## Argentina, Uruguay and Colombia: nature between major cities

You can choose an itinerary visiting [Argentina](/argentina/), [Uruguay](/uruguay/) and [Colombia](/colombia/), but the nature experiences offered in these countries vary considerably on the current tour. Argentina brings the famous Iguazu Falls, Colombia offers the views around Guatapé and El Peñón rock, while Uruguay is included primarily for a visit to Montevideo.

Our selection includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}}. This is an [extensive 32-day itinerary through eight South American countries](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/). Selecting these three countries does not mean a short trip between Buenos Aires, Montevideo and Colombia alone. The programme includes Chile, Bolivia, Peru and Ecuador between the days in Uruguay and Colombia.

## Argentina: Iguazu as the main nature excursion

After seeing the falls from Brazil, travellers visit the Argentine sector near [Puerto Iguazú](/argentina/place/puerto-iguazu/). This is one of the most important nature days of the entire journey. The viewing trails reveal the river system, powerful cascades, lush vegetation and humid forest around them. Seeing both sides of the border gives visitors a fuller impression of the same natural landmark.

Argentina's Iguazú National Park is a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Its importance comes from both the waterfalls and the protection of a substantial area of subtropical Atlantic Forest. Even a short visit here is therefore quite different from seeing a single urban attraction. The programme does not, however, promise a separate safari or guaranteed sightings of particular animal species.

The group then travels to [Buenos Aires](/argentina/place/buenos-aires/), where the programme includes a city tour, the San Telmo and La Boca neighbourhoods, and an evening of tango. Patagonia and the glaciers of southern Argentina are not part of this tour. This matters especially to nature enthusiasts, since the name Argentina often brings to mind mountain and glacier journeys that are not included here.

## Uruguay: a short city visit to Montevideo

[Montevideo](/uruguay/place/montevideo/) is scheduled as a **day trip from Buenos Aires**. The itinerary includes an early transfer to the port, a ferry crossing, a guided sightseeing tour of Uruguay's capital with an English-speaking guide, and the return to Argentina. This is a very different way of visiting a country from a multiday nature-focused stay.

The crossing gives travellers a sense of the geography of the Río de la Plata estuary, but the itinerary does not include a separate expedition to Uruguay's reserves or extensive natural areas. The Uruguayan day focuses on city squares, the historic centre and a walk around [Montevideo](/uruguay/place/montevideo/). Without corresponding activities, it should not be described as a beach holiday or a national park excursion.

If exploring Uruguay's natural landscapes is a major priority, this tour allows little time for that. Extending the visit would require a separate discussion of dates, transport and arrangements; no such extension is part of the published 32-day programme.

## Colombia: Guatapé rock, mountain scenery and cities

After a long journey across western South America, the tour reaches Colombia. Near [Medellín](/colombia/place/medellin/), travellers visit [Guatapé](/colombia/place/guatape/) and [El Peñón de Guatapé](/colombia/place/el-penon-de-guatape/). The dominant natural features here are a towering rock formation, hills and surrounding water. This is neither Iguazu's humid lowland forest nor the estuary around Montevideo, but a different mountain landscape elsewhere on the continent.

The itinerary continues to Cartagena and Bogotá. From [Monserrate](/colombia/place/monserrate-bogota/), visitors can appreciate the mountains surrounding the capital. The Monserrate visit is included in a city sightseeing day, however, as are the other Bogotá excursions; there is no separate multiday trek in Colombia. Cartagena is likewise presented as a historic city rather than an extended marine wildlife cruise.

This balance makes the route suitable for travellers who enjoy alternating major natural landmarks with iconic cities. Someone interested exclusively in national parks may find a 32-day journey through eight countries less closely tailored to that goal.

## Comparing the three countries within the complete itinerary

| Stop | What the itinerary includes |
|---|---|
| [Argentina](/argentina/) | The Argentine side of Iguazu Falls, followed by urban Buenos Aires |
| [Uruguay](/uruguay/) | One day in Montevideo with a ferry crossing and sightseeing tour |
| [Colombia](/colombia/) | Guatapé, El Peñón rock, cities and views around Bogotá |

{{catalog.tourTable:tour_south_america_eight_countries_32_days_2026}}

The full programme adds far richer nature destinations outside the selected three countries: Bolivia's high-altitude lagoons and Uyuni, Lake Titicaca in Peru, and Ecuador's Galápagos Islands. These days add considerable value to the overall tour, but they cannot be counted as nature experiences in Uruguay.

If your main goal is Iguazu and visiting Uruguay and Colombia would be welcome additions, this itinerary makes sense. If you want to spend many days immersed in nature in each of the three countries, a more specialised programme would be preferable.

## Weather, crossings and extensive travel logistics

The route includes a water crossing between Buenos Aires and Montevideo, so transport schedules and weather conditions affect the length of that day. After Uruguay, the journey continues to Chile and across the Andes. It then moves through high-altitude and island environments before reaching Colombia. Packing for such changing climates is significant: the humid Iguazu region, cooler highlands and warm Caribbean coast call for different clothing.

Spray protection and nonslip footwear are useful at Iguazu, comfortable clothing for extended walks is helpful in cities, and warm layers are needed for the high-altitude sections of the full journey. Altitude tolerance and physical exertion should be considered when planning, even though the days in Argentina and Uruguay are mainly sightseeing days.

Visa and transit rules need to be checked for all eight countries and for each traveller's nationality. Argentina, Uruguay and Colombia use different national currencies; Colombia's currency is the Colombian peso. Whether an international bank card will work depends on the issuer and the individual service provider. Ada Tours can help coordinate flights, excursions, the ferry crossing and the breakdown of expenses, while the terms of each leg depend on the actual bookings.

Other itineraries involving these countries can be found in the [general Argentina–Colombia–Uruguay catalogue](/multi-country/argentina_colombia_uruguay/). For nature-focused journeys across the continent, see our [selection of multicountry nature tours](/multi-country/interests/nature/).

## Frequently asked questions about combining these three countries

### How many days are spent in Uruguay on this tour?

The current programme includes **one day** in Montevideo, with a ferry from Buenos Aires and a sightseeing excursion. A separate multiday journey through Uruguay is not included.

### Does the itinerary visit Argentine Patagonia?

No. The main nature attraction on the Argentine leg is Iguazu, followed by Buenos Aires. Patagonia is not on the published itinerary.

### Which nature attractions are included in Colombia?

The [Guatapé and El Peñón area](/colombia/place/el-penon-de-guatape/) and views from Monserrate near Bogotá. There is no dedicated multiday nature trek.

### Why does the 'Nature' filter include urban Montevideo?

Because the theme applies to the **entire 32-day tour**, while the selected combination identifies countries visited on that route. Check the activities planned for each individual country before choosing.

## Where can you observe animals on this three-country route?

Our 'Wildlife and Safari' selection for Argentina, Colombia and Uruguay includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}}. One option is the [extensive 32-day journey through South America](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/). It crosses eight countries, so it is important to distinguish **wildlife watching on the complete itinerary** from the actual activities offered in each country you have selected in the filter.

In Argentina, an excursion visits Iguazu Falls, surrounded by humid Atlantic Forest. Uruguay is represented by a brief city visit to Montevideo. In Colombia, the most dramatic scenic excursion takes travellers to El Peñón rock and the Guatapé reservoir. This programme does not advertise specialised wildlife watching in Uruguay or Colombia. A substantial part of the full journey's wildlife experiences is connected with **Ecuador's Galápagos Islands**, outside the selected three-country combination.

This is a good example of why a country list alone is insufficient when choosing a safari or birdwatching trip. If you simply want these three countries without a wildlife focus, see the [general Argentina + Colombia + Uruguay catalogue](/multi-country/argentina_colombia_uruguay/). For other multicountry wildlife formats, explore the ['Wildlife and Safari' catalogue](/multi-country/interests/wildlife/). If waterfalls and mountain views interest you more, see [this combination under the 'Nature' theme](/multi-country/argentina_colombia_uruguay/interests/nature/).

## Iguazu in Argentina: a real national park, without guaranteed encounters

Near [Puerto Iguazú](/argentina/place/puerto-iguazu/), travellers visit the Argentine side of the waterfalls. The national park protects a large area of subtropical forest with diverse animal and bird life. Toucans, coatis and large forest mammals are among the species associated with the region, although an animal's presence in an ecosystem does not guarantee a sighting on any particular day.

The group excursion with a Russian-speaking guide focuses on the waterfalls and walks along the park's visitor trails. A flight to [Buenos Aires](/argentina/place/buenos-aires/) follows, so this leg includes no separate overnight stay for prolonged birdwatching or night photography in the forest.

Conditions on the trails matter as much as the season. Rainfall and river levels affect access to the Iguazu viewpoints; in 2026, Argentine park officials temporarily restricted access to the Devil's Throat because of rising water. Current restrictions should be checked immediately before the visit. On the neighbouring Brazilian side, the Bird Park and Macuco Safari may be available as optional activities, but they are listed **as additional paid services**, not as an included Argentine wildlife day.

For itineraries with longer stays in natural environments, compare [nature-themed tours in Argentina](/interests/nature/tours/argentina/).

## Uruguay: a ferry excursion to a city, not a nature expedition

One day is allocated to Uruguay. The group takes a ferry from Buenos Aires across the Río de la Plata, explores [Montevideo](/uruguay/place/montevideo/) and returns to Argentina. The programme lists the port, Independence Square, the old town and the cathedral. An English-speaking guide leads the sightseeing tour, and ferry tickets are included.

The crossing itself provides an interesting view of the estuary and coastal landscape from the water. However, **this is regular transport within a city excursion, not a whale- or dolphin-watching cruise**. The itinerary includes no separate Uruguayan reserve, lagoon expedition, organised fishing trip or birdwatching activity. It would be misleading to promise these experiences solely because the full tour has a wildlife theme.

The trade-off of a long journey is especially clear here: another country adds cultural variety but does not increase the number of days spent observing wildlife. Including natural sites in Uruguay would require a different allocation of time and a prearranged itinerary. ## Where the complete itinerary really explores island wildlife

After visiting Quito in Ecuador, the programme travels to the [Galápagos Islands](/ecuador/place/galapagos-islands/). A visit to the highlands of [Santa Cruz](/ecuador/place/santa-cruz-island/) is scheduled. The option is confirmed at booking.

This is far closer to what travellers expect from a wildlife trip. The islands are known for seabirds, iguanas, tortoises and sea lions; some animals can be watched at relatively close range, but interacting with them is prohibited. Protected areas have rules on behaviour, guided visits and minimum distances. Specific species, weather and sea conditions cannot be guaranteed in advance.

If your goal is to **combine Iguazu and the Galápagos**, consider the full eight-country route with its separate Ecuadorian leg. ## Argentina and Ecuador: what route does Ada Tours offer?

Our selection for Argentina and Ecuador includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}}. It is [“Eight South American Countries in 32 Days: From Rio and Iguazu to the Galápagos and Colombia”](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/), scheduled from October 22 to November 22, 2026. Its main countries are Brazil, Argentina, Uruguay, Chile, Bolivia, Peru, Ecuador and Colombia.

{{catalog.tourTable:tour_south_america_eight_countries_32_days_2026}}

**Argentina and Ecuador are separated by almost two weeks of other experiences on the itinerary.** On the Argentine leg, travellers visit Iguazu and Buenos Aires, then travel to Montevideo before continuing to Chile. Ecuador is reached only on day 21, with the flight from Lima to Quito. This tour is therefore designed for an extensive exploration of the continent, not a short holiday restricted to the two countries named here.

| Stage | Days of the journey |
|---|---|
| Argentina | 7–10 |
| Chile, Bolivia, Peru | 10–20 |
| Ecuador | 21–25 |
| Then Colombia | 26–32 |

Day 10 includes a flight from Buenos Aires to Chile. These date ranges must not be presented as separate tour packages: they are sections of one continuous programme.

## Argentina: Iguazu Falls and Buenos Aires

The Argentine part follows Brazil. On day 6, the group sees Iguazu Falls from the Brazilian side, and **on day 7 visits the Argentine side**, following a national park route near [Puerto Iguazú](/argentina/place/puerto-iguazu/). The two sides provide different views of the waterfalls and require planning for a border crossing. After the excursion, the group flies to [Buenos Aires](/argentina/place/buenos-aires/).

Day 8 includes a three-hour tour of the capital with a Russian-speaking guide. In the evening, a tango show with dinner is part of the programme. The following day, travellers cross the Río de la Plata by ferry for a sightseeing excursion in [Montevideo](/uruguay/place/montevideo/), returning to Argentina afterwards. This is a visit to Uruguay, so the country's travel documents and border requirements need to be considered alongside those of the other destinations.

Day 10 begins the next geographical stage with a flight from Buenos Aires to Santiago, Chile. **There is no direct Argentina–Ecuador flight within the published itinerary.** Before arriving in Quito, travellers visit the Atacama Desert, high-altitude lagoons, Uyuni, Lake Titicaca, Cusco and Machu Picchu.

### How this differs from a dedicated trip to Argentina

The Argentine section comprises several sightseeing days and does not include an extended journey into Patagonia. If you want glaciers, Ushuaia or a dedicated route through Argentina's regions, see the [Argentina tours catalogue](/argentina/tour/). The Argentina + Ecuador selection represents **only the actual shared geography** of the current multicountry tour; it does not promise all the main attractions of either country.

## How the journey from Argentina to Ecuador unfolds

The planned order is purposeful: cities and waterfalls first, then increasingly high-altitude terrain, and finally the oceanic islands.

After flying to Chile, the group visits Santiago, then flies to Calama and travels to [San Pedro de Atacama](/chile/place/san-pedro-de-atacama/). This stop also provides an opportunity to adjust before the altitudes of Bolivia. A nighttime astronomy excursion is offered separately and must not be assumed to be included.

Next comes **a two-day 4×4 jeep route through Bolivia**, with high-altitude lagoons, geothermal features, salt flats and [Uyuni](/bolivia/place/uyuni/). Some sections exceed 4,000 metres in elevation. This can be more physically demanding than ordinary city sightseeing: the schedule involves long drives, early departures and nights in expedition-style conditions.

The route then continues through La Paz, crosses into Peru near Desaguadero, and visits Lake Titicaca, Cusco and [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/). After a sightseeing tour of Lima comes **day 21: the Lima–Quito flight**, which begins the Ecuadorian leg.

A standalone Argentina + Ecuador itinerary would therefore need a completely different flight plan. Shortening the full tour is not simply a matter of deleting the intermediate days: overnight stays, air tickets, the order of excursions and the cost would all change.

## Ecuador: high-altitude Quito and the oceanic Galápagos

[Quito](/ecuador/place/quito-and-cotopaxi-volcano/) lies in the Andes at an elevation of approximately 2,800 metres. After arrival from Lima, a transfer to the hotel is scheduled. The next day includes the historic centre, [Mitad del Mundo](/ecuador/place/mitad-del-mundo/) near the equator and the [Intiñan Museum](/ecuador/place/intinan-museum/).

On day 23, the group flies to the [Galápagos Islands](/ecuador/place/galapagos-islands/). The programme specifies arrival at the airport on [Baltra](/ecuador/place/baltra-island/). Travellers then cross the Itabaca Channel to [Santa Cruz](/ecuador/place/santa-cruz-island/) and visit its highland area. Accommodation is on the islands, rather than on a multiday sea cruise.

Day 24 offers **one of two alternative marine excursions**: North Seymour and Bachas, or South Plaza and Cape Carrión. One option is confirmed after booking. This choice matters particularly to travellers interested in birds, marine animals and coastal environments: the specific islands visited determine the experiences on the day. Both alternatives cannot be treated as simultaneously included.

Day 25 brings the return to the mainland and a flight to [Guayaquil](/ecuador/place/guayaquil/). Departure from Ecuador for Colombia is scheduled on day 26. **There is no separate multiday stop in the Ecuadorian Amazon on this itinerary.** If you are particularly interested in the Amazon or other parts of Ecuador, compare [tours of Ecuador](/ecuador/tour/) with this multicountry programme.

## Galápagos: special requirements and additional costs

Visiting the Galápagos requires special entry procedures even for travellers already in Ecuador. Before departing from the mainland, visitors arrange a **Transit Control Card (TCT)** and undergo biosecurity baggage checks. On arrival, a conservation entrance fee is payable according to the visitor category. These procedures differ from standard passport control on arrival in mainland Ecuador.

When considering an Argentina and Ecuador tour, clarify in advance:

- who arranges the TCT information and what documents are needed before flying to the archipelago;
- how the conservation fee and other local charges are treated in the list of included services;
- which of the two marine excursions has been confirmed for the travel date;
- what baggage and transport requirements apply to flights between Quito, Baltra and Guayaquil.

The Galápagos have restrictions on bringing in plants, organic products and other items that could affect island ecosystems. If your journey begins in Argentina and crosses several countries, **do not carry food or natural souvenirs onward to the islands without checking the rules**.

The actual flights and excursions are listed in the current tour. Fees should be confirmed separately: a general statement that 'all admission tickets in the programme' are included cannot automatically be interpreted to cover every mandatory government charge.

## Spring in Argentina in October and November in the Galápagos

The two countries have different climatic patterns. Late October is spring in Argentina. The Iguazu region is humid and subtropical, while [Buenos Aires](/argentina/place/buenos-aires/) usually has more comfortable temperatures for long city walks. Rain is possible in both places.

In Ecuador, altitude and proximity to the ocean matter more than the familiar four European seasons. Quito is cooler, especially in the mornings and evenings. In the Galápagos, **November falls within the cooler period** associated with the influence of the Humboldt Current. This affects water temperatures and what to wear on boat trips, although sunshine and conditions still vary between individual islands.

Packing for one 32-day journey means preparing for four situations: wet paths at Iguazu, spring weather in Buenos Aires, cold high-altitude areas of Bolivia and marine excursions in the Galápagos. Clothing for Quito and the Galápagos will also differ, even though both stops are in Ecuador.

**Allow for time zone changes and flight schedules.** Between the Argentine section and arrival in Ecuador, travellers change countries and communications conditions several times. The total number of nights on a tour does not automatically indicate how much free time is available each day: some days are partly or entirely taken up by transfers.

## Documents, currencies, budget and insurance

Argentina uses the Argentine peso, while Ecuador uses the US dollar. The published route also passes through six other countries with their own payment arrangements and local currencies. Check in advance which expenses are payable in USD, which are paid locally, where cash reserves will be needed and which bank cards a particular traveller can use.

Visa and migration requirements must be assessed **for all eight countries**, not just Argentina and Ecuador. This includes nationality, passports, possible visas, transit requirements, flight dates and documents needed for land-border crossings. The Galápagos TCT is an additional formality. It would be incorrect to assume that one permit is sufficient for all of South America.

Travel insurance needs to cover the countries and activities actually included in the journey. Bolivia's high-altitude sections and jeep travel deserve particular attention when selecting coverage. Anyone with relevant health concerns should discuss tolerance for high altitude and travel conditions with a doctor. Island excursions take place in a different natural environment, and insurance should also be appropriate for the planned marine activities.

### Is there a ready-made tour covering only Argentina and Ecuador?

Day 7 includes the Argentine side of Iguazu and a flight to Buenos Aires; day 8 covers a city excursion and tango with dinner. Day 9 is a return ferry excursion to Montevideo. The flight to Chile takes place on day 10.

Because the route crosses Chile, Bolivia and Peru in sequence, with separate excursions, high-altitude terrain, Uyuni, Titicaca and Machu Picchu. Ecuador begins only after the flight from Lima, with another seven days in Colombia following it.
